title: More practice · C1
desc: Extra exercises for each C1 unit.
intro: One topic for each part of the unit. Each practice brings ALL the exercises of the topic: first the ones you got wrong, then the new ones.

sets.title: Narrative tenses and the past perfect continuous
sets.intro: Good stories mix the past simple, past continuous, past perfect and past perfect continuous. Use had been + -ing for an activity that was going on up to a moment in the past, and the simple form for results, numbers and state verbs.

watch.wrong: I was waiting for two hours when she finally arrived.
watch.right: I had been waiting for two hours when she finally arrived.
watch.why: Duration before a past moment needs had been + -ing.

watch.wrong: By then, she had been knowing the city for years.
watch.right: By then, she had known the city for years.
watch.why: Know is stative: no continuous.

watch.wrong: When we got there, the guests already left.
watch.right: When we got there, the guests had already left.
watch.why: Earlier action: past perfect.

items.prompt: By the time the bus came, we ___ for forty minutes in the rain. (wait)
answers: had been waiting
items.explain: Duration up to a past moment: past perfect continuous.

items.prompt: Her eyes were red because she ___ all night. (cry)
answers: had been crying
items.explain: The activity continued up to the moment we describe, and we can see its result.

items.prompt: She was exhausted. She ___ since five in the morning. (work)
answers: had been working
items.explain: Since + a starting point shows duration before a past moment.

items.prompt: When the manager walked in, the staff ___ about the new schedule for an hour. (argue)
answers: had been arguing
items.explain: Long activity before the manager arrived: had been + -ing.

items.prompt: By noon, he ___ three reports. (write)
answers: had written
items.explain: A specific number points to the result, so we use the simple form.

items.prompt: It ___ all morning, so the streets were flooded. (rain)
answers: had been raining
items.explain: Continuous activity with a visible result in the past.

items.prompt: We were late because we ___ the wrong train. (take)
answers: had taken
items.explain: A single completed earlier action: past perfect simple.

items.prompt: I was irritable because I ___ well for weeks. (negative, sleep)
answers: hadn't been sleeping
had not been sleeping
items.explain: Negative duration before a past moment: hadn't been + -ing.

items.prompt: While the guests were chatting, the chef quietly ___ the dessert. (burn)
answers: burned
burnt
items.explain: The past simple moves the story forward.

items.prompt: ___ they been living abroad long before they moved back?
answers: Had

items.prompt: My hands were covered in paint because I ___ the fence. (paint)
answers: had been painting
items.explain: Activity before a past moment that left a trace.

items.prompt: She ___ the letter before she realised it was addressed to someone else. (open)
answers: had opened
items.explain: One completed earlier action: past perfect simple.

items.prompt: When the lights went out, the audience ___ in silence for ten minutes. (sit)
answers: had been sitting
items.explain: Duration before a past moment: had been sitting.

items.prompt: She looked tired. She ___ since dawn.
items.explain: Since dawn shows duration up to a past moment.

items.prompt: By then, I ___ the answer for years.
items.explain: Know is a stative verb: no continuous form.

items.prompt: He ___ five emails by nine o'clock.
items.explain: A number of completed items needs the simple form.

items.prompt: When we arrived, the match ___.
items.explain: The match started earlier: past perfect.

items.prompt: Just as I stepped outside, I noticed it ___.
items.explain: Background action in progress: past continuous.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: She had been waiting for hours when he called.
She was been waiting for hours when he called.
She had been wait for hours when he called.

items.prompt: We had been wait for an hour when the doors opened.
answers: We had been waiting for an hour when the doors opened.
items.explain: Had been is followed by the -ing form.

items.prompt: She had been owning the shop for ten years when it burned down.
answers: She had owned the shop for ten years when it burned down.
items.explain: Own is a stative verb: it does not take the continuous.

items.prompt: When I got home, my flatmates already ate everything.
answers: When I got home, my flatmates had already eaten everything.
items.explain: An earlier past action needs the past perfect.

items.prompt: They has been arguing for hours when I arrived.
answers: They had been arguing for hours when I arrived.
items.explain: Use had (not has) for all persons in the past perfect.

items.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: She had been studying for hours before the power went out.
items.explain: Had been studying shows duration before the power cut.

items.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: I had never seen him so angry before that day.
items.explain: Past perfect for an experience before a past moment.

items.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: The ground was wet because it had been raining all night.
items.explain: Had been raining explains the wet ground.

items.prompt: Estaba agotada porque había estado cuidando a su hermano toda la semana.
answers: She was exhausted because she had been looking after her brother all week.
She was exhausted because she had been taking care of her brother all week.
items.explain: Duration before a past moment: had been + -ing.

items.prompt: Cuando llegué, ya se habían ido todos.
answers: When I arrived, everyone had already left.
When I arrived, everybody had already left.
When I arrived, they had all left.
When I arrived, everyone had already gone.
items.explain: Completed action before another past action: past perfect.

items.prompt: Llevábamos horas caminando cuando por fin vimos el pueblo.
answers: We had been walking for hours when we finally saw the village.
We had been walking for hours when we finally saw the town.
items.explain: Had been walking for hours: duration before a past event.

items.prompt: La tienda ya había cerrado cuando llegamos.
answers: The shop had already closed when we arrived.
The store had already closed when we arrived.
The shop had closed when we arrived.
items.explain: Past perfect for the earlier event.

sets.title: Used to, would, be used to and get used to
sets.intro: Used to + base and would + base describe past habits. Be used to and get used to mean 'accustomed to', and the word to is a preposition, so a noun or -ing form follows.

watch.wrong: I'm not used to wake up so early.
watch.right: I'm not used to waking up so early.
watch.why: To is a preposition in be used to.

watch.wrong: She didn't used to like coffee.
watch.right: She didn't use to like coffee.
watch.why: After didn't, base form: use to.

watch.wrong: In my twenties I would be very insecure.
watch.right: In my twenties I used to be very insecure.
watch.why: Be is stative: would is not possible.

items.prompt: When I was a kid, my uncle ___ tell us ghost stories every summer night. (would)
answers: would
items.explain: Would can describe repeated past actions once the time is clear.

items.prompt: She ___ have long hair, but now it is short. (a past state)
answers: used to
items.explain: Have (possession) is a state: only used to works.

items.prompt: I'm not used to ___ in such a noisy city. (live)
answers: living

items.prompt: It took him months to get used to ___ on the left. (drive)
answers: driving

items.prompt: Did you ___ to play the piano as a child? (use)
answers: use
items.explain: After did, the verb is use, without -d.

items.prompt: We never ___ to eat out; my mother cooked everything.
answers: used
items.explain: Never used to + base describes a past habit.

items.prompt: I'm slowly getting ___ to the altitude here.
answers: used
items.explain: Get used to = become accustomed to.

items.prompt: Years ago this street ___ be full of small shops.
answers: used to
items.explain: Be is a state verb, so would is impossible.

items.prompt: He's a pilot, so he is used to ___ up very early. (get)
answers: getting

items.prompt: Our company ___ to hold its meetings on Fridays, but now they are on Mondays. (use)
answers: used
items.explain: Used to + base: a past habit that has ended.

items.prompt: I'm not used ___ spicy food; it makes my eyes water.
answers: to
items.explain: Be used to + noun: to is a preposition.

items.prompt: Don't worry; you will ___ used to the new software in a couple of days. (get)
answers: get
items.explain: Get used to = gradually become accustomed.

items.prompt: Stop shouting. I'm not used to ___ spoken to like that. (be)
answers: being
items.explain: Be used to + being + past participle.

items.prompt: I ___ a motorbike when I was a student.
items.explain: Have = possess is a state: used to.

items.prompt: She isn't used to ___ alone.
When we were kids, we ___ build dens in the woods every weekend.
It's taking me time to ___ the heat.
items.explain: After to: get used to + noun.

items.prompt: I ___ in Lima for six years before moving to Quito.
items.explain: A closed period with a duration needs the past simple.

items.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: He didn't use to like olives.
He didn't used to like olives.
He not used to like olives.
items.explain: After didn't, use the base form: use to.

items.prompt: I'm not used to wake up before seven.
answers: I'm not used to waking up before seven.
I am not used to waking up before seven.
items.explain: In be used to, to is a preposition: -ing follows.

items.prompt: When I was young I would be afraid of the dark.
answers: When I was young I used to be afraid of the dark.
items.explain: Be is a state: use used to.

items.prompt: She didn't used to drink coffee.
answers: She didn't use to drink coffee.
She did not use to drink coffee.
items.explain: After didn't the verb is in base form.

items.prompt: We were used to spend summers at my aunt's farm when I was a boy.
answers: We used to spend summers at my aunt's farm when I was a boy.
items.explain: A finished past habit: used to + base.

items.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: It took me a while to get used to the noise.
items.explain: Get used to + noun describes a process.

items.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: My father used to take us fishing on Saturdays.

items.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: I'm still not used to living on my own.

items.prompt: Antes vivía cerca del mar, pero ahora vivo en la montaña.
answers: I used to live near the sea, but now I live in the mountains.
I used to live by the sea, but now I live in the mountains.
I used to live near the sea, but now I live in the mountain.
items.explain: Used to + base for a past state.

items.prompt: No estoy acostumbrado a levantarme tan temprano.
answers: I'm not used to getting up so early.
I am not used to getting up so early.
I'm not used to waking up so early.
I am not used to waking up so early.

items.prompt: Poco a poco te acostumbrarás al ruido.
answers: You'll get used to the noise little by little.
You will get used to the noise little by little.
You'll get used to the noise gradually.
You will get used to the noise gradually.
You'll get used to the noise in time.
You will get used to the noise in time.
items.explain: Get used to = the process of becoming accustomed.

items.prompt: De niños, cada verano íbamos a la playa con mis abuelos.
answers: As children, every summer we would go to the beach with our grandparents.
As children, we used to go to the beach with our grandparents every summer.
When we were kids, we would go to the beach with our grandparents every summer.
When we were kids, we used to go to the beach with our grandparents every summer.
items.explain: Used to or would for repeated past actions.

sets.title: Describing people with nuance
sets.intro: At C1 you grade and soften descriptions. Use softeners (rather, somewhat, a touch), understatement (not exactly), impression verbs (come across as, strike me as) and absolutely/utterly with extreme adjectives.

watch.wrong: He's very exhausted after the flight.
watch.right: He's absolutely exhausted after the flight.
watch.why: Extreme adjectives take absolutely or utterly.

watch.wrong: She came across as arrogantly.
watch.right: She came across as arrogant.
watch.why: Come across as + adjective.

watch.wrong: She made me an impression of being very honest.
watch.right: She gave me the impression of being very honest.
watch.why: Give someone the impression of.

items.prompt: She was ___ furious when she saw the bill. (a word that reinforces an extreme adjective)
answers: absolutely
utterly
completely
totally
items.explain: Extreme adjectives take absolutely, utterly or completely, not very.

items.prompt: He doesn't ___ across as very friendly at first, but he is.
answers: come
items.explain: Come across as = give the impression of being.

items.prompt: She ___ me as rather shy, though I only spoke to her for a minute. (strike, past)
answers: struck

items.prompt: She's not ___ the most patient person in the office. (understatement)
answers: exactly
really
items.explain: Not exactly the most + adjective: ironic understatement.

items.prompt: He gave me the ___ of being a man with something to hide.
answers: impression
items.explain: Give someone the impression of / that.

items.prompt: Julia seems ___ be a little anxious today.
answers: to

items.prompt: My new colleague is ___ reserved; she rarely speaks in meetings. (softener)
answers: rather
fairly
somewhat
quite
slightly
a bit
a little
pretty
relatively
items.explain: A softener makes the description less direct.

items.prompt: Her feedback can be a ___ too blunt at times.
answers: touch
bit
little
items.explain: A touch too + adjective is a gentle criticism.

items.prompt: At first she struck me ___ arrogant, but she is just shy.
answers: as

items.prompt: Their new manager comes across ___ very approachable.
answers: as

items.prompt: He made a lasting impression ___ everyone he met.
answers: on

items.prompt: She has a way of ___ everyone feel at ease. (make)
answers: making

items.prompt: I couldn't ___ been more wrong about him; he's wonderful.
answers: have
items.explain: Couldn't have been more wrong = completely wrong.

items.prompt: The hotel room was ___ freezing.
She came across as ___.
items.explain: Come across as takes an adjective.

items.prompt: Which is the gentlest way to criticise?
He ___ me as a bit self-important.
She gave me the impression ___ being honest.
'He's not exactly generous' most probably means that he is ___.
items.explain: Not exactly + adjective often says the opposite, politely.

items.prompt: She came across as arrogantly in the interview.
answers: She came across as arrogant in the interview.
items.explain: Come across as + adjective, not adverb.

items.prompt: He is very exhausted after the long flight.
answers: He is absolutely exhausted after the long flight.
He is utterly exhausted after the long flight.
He is completely exhausted after the long flight.
He is totally exhausted after the long flight.
items.explain: Exhausted is extreme: it is not used with very.

items.prompt: She made me the impression of being rather cold.
answers: She gave me the impression of being rather cold.
items.explain: The collocation is give someone the impression of.

items.prompt: He strikes to me as rather insecure.
answers: He strikes me as rather insecure.
items.explain: Strike takes a direct object: strike me as.

items.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: She comes across as rather confident.

items.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: He's not exactly the most patient person.

items.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: At first he struck me as somewhat distant.

items.prompt: Me pareció un poco reservado al principio.
answers: He struck me as a bit reserved at first.
He struck me as a little reserved at first.
He seemed a bit reserved at first.
He seemed a little reserved at first.
He came across as a bit reserved at first.

items.prompt: Su hermana da la impresión de ser muy segura de sí misma.
answers: Her sister gives the impression of being very self-confident.
Her sister gives the impression of being very self-assured.
Her sister comes across as very self-confident.
Her sister comes across as very self-assured.
Her sister comes across as very confident.
Her sister gives the impression of being very confident.
items.explain: Give the impression of + -ing / come across as + adjective.

items.prompt: No es precisamente la persona más puntual.
answers: He's not exactly the most punctual person.
He is not exactly the most punctual person.
She's not exactly the most punctual person.
She is not exactly the most punctual person.

items.prompt: Estaba absolutamente agotado después del viaje.
answers: I was absolutely exhausted after the trip.
I was absolutely exhausted after the journey.
He was absolutely exhausted after the trip.
He was absolutely exhausted after the journey.

sets.title: Personality compounds and first-meeting expressions
sets.intro: These words and phrases help you describe character and tell stories about meeting people.

learn.def: easily made angry
learn.example: He's so quick-tempered that nobody dares to disagree with him.

learn.def: forgetful because you think about other things
learn.example: My absent-minded aunt put the milk in the cupboard.

learn.def: willing to consider new ideas
learn.example: A good teacher stays open-minded about different approaches.

learn.def: unwilling to accept other views
learn.example: It is narrow-minded to judge people by their accent.

learn.def: too proud of your own abilities
learn.example: Winning the prize made him a little big-headed.

learn.def: not easily upset by criticism
learn.example: Politicians need to be thick-skinned.

learn.def: calm and sensible in difficult situations
learn.example: She stayed level-headed during the emergency.

learn.def: relaxed and not easily worried
learn.example: Our easy-going landlord never minds late rent for a few days.

learn.def: do something to make people feel relaxed
learn.example: A quick round of introductions broke the ice.

learn.def: get on well with someone immediately
learn.example: The two chefs hit it off over a shared love of spices.

learn.def: without any warning
learn.example: An old friend called me out of the blue.

learn.def: be surprised and slightly shocked
learn.example: I was taken aback by how direct the question was.

answers: She is so absent-minded that she left her keys in the fridge.

items.prompt: Put the words in order.

answers: He's very easy-going and never gets upset about anything.

answers: Her message came out of the blue and I was taken aback.
His message came out of the blue and I was taken aback.

sets.title: Future perfect simple and continuous
sets.intro: The future perfect looks back from a point in the future. Use will have + past participle for what will be finished by then, and will have been + -ing for a duration that reaches that point. By means 'no later than'; until means 'up to'.

watch.wrong: By the time I will finish, they will have left.
watch.right: By the time I finish, they will have left.
watch.why: Present simple after by the time.

watch.wrong: By next June I will work here for ten years.
watch.right: By next June I will have been working here for ten years.
watch.why: Duration up to a future point: future perfect.

watch.wrong: I will finish the report until Friday.
watch.right: I will finish the report by Friday.
watch.why: By = no later than.

items.prompt: By the end of this year, I ___ in this company for a decade. (work)
answers: will have been working
will have worked
items.explain: Duration up to a future point: future perfect.

items.prompt: By the time you read this, I ___ the exam. (finish)
answers: will have finished
items.explain: An action completed before a future point.

items.prompt: By the time the guests arrive, we ___ dinner. (prepare)
answers: will have prepared
will have been preparing
items.explain: Future perfect: finished before the guests come.

items.prompt: I will have repaid the loan ___ 2030.
answers: by
items.explain: By = no later than a time.

items.prompt: I'll wait here ___ Friday, and then I'll leave.
answers: until
till
items.explain: Until = up to a time, with a situation that continues.

items.prompt: By the time I ___ home, they will have eaten. (get)
answers: get
items.explain: After by the time, use the present simple, not will.

items.prompt: In two years' time, he ___ his degree. (complete)
answers: will have completed

items.prompt: By next summer, she ___ for the same firm for fifteen years. (work)
answers: will have been working
will have worked

items.prompt: By this time next year, ___ they have moved to Chile?
answers: will
items.explain: Question form: will + subject + have + past participle.

items.prompt: They ___ the bridge before the rainy season starts. (negative, finish)
answers: won't have finished
will not have finished
items.explain: Negative future perfect: won't have + past participle.

items.prompt: By midnight, the team ___ for sixteen hours straight. (work)
answers: will have been working
will have worked
items.explain: Duration up to a future point.

items.prompt: By the time I retire, I ___ over three thousand patients. (treat)
answers: will have treated
items.explain: A specific number points to the simple form.

items.prompt: Before long, robots ___ half of these tasks. (take over)
answers: will have taken over
items.explain: Completed before an unspecified future point.

items.prompt: By 2035 the city ___ its entire bus fleet.
items.explain: Future perfect with a by + date marker.

items.prompt: I'll stay in Lima ___ the end of June.
items.explain: Until = a situation that continues up to that time.

items.prompt: By then, they ___ married for twenty years.
items.explain: Will have + past participle of be.

items.prompt: By the time she ___, the film will have started.
items.explain: Present simple after by the time.

items.prompt: Next year I ___ here for a decade; that's why I'm celebrating.
items.explain: Duration up to a future point.

items.prompt: Which sentence stresses the process rather than the result?
options: By June I will have been writing the book for a year.
By June I will have written the book.
By June I will write the book.
items.explain: Will have been + -ing focuses on the activity.

items.prompt: By the time we will arrive, the shop will have closed.
answers: By the time we arrive, the shop will have closed.
items.explain: After by the time, use the present simple.

items.prompt: By next month she will work here for five years.
answers: By next month she will have been working here for five years.
By next month she will have worked here for five years.
items.explain: Duration up to a future point needs the future perfect.

items.prompt: He will have been knowing her for ten years by then.
answers: He will have known her for ten years by then.

items.prompt: I will finish the project until Monday.
answers: I will finish the project by Monday.
items.explain: By = no later than; until = up to.

items.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: By then she will have been living abroad for a decade.
items.explain: Future perfect continuous: duration up to a future point.

items.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: We will have finished the survey by the end of the week.

items.prompt: Put the words in order.
answers: They won't have repaired the road by next month.

items.prompt: Para el viernes ya habré terminado el informe.
answers: By Friday I will have finished the report.
By Friday I'll have finished the report.
I will have finished the report by Friday.
I'll have finished the report by Friday.
items.explain: Will have + past participle with by.

items.prompt: El próximo mes llevaré diez años viviendo en esta ciudad.
answers: Next month I will have been living in this city for ten years.
Next month I'll have been living in this city for ten years.
Next month I will have lived in this city for ten years.
Next month I'll have lived in this city for ten years.
items.explain: Duration up to a future point.

items.prompt: Cuando llegues, ya se habrán ido.
answers: By the time you arrive, they will have left.
By the time you arrive, they'll have left.
When you arrive, they will have left.
When you arrive, they'll have left.

items.prompt: ¿Habrás terminado para las cinco?

sets.title: Collocations for proposing solutions
sets.intro: Strong essays use precise verb + noun collocations when proposing solutions. Learn them as chunks: tackle a problem, curb emissions, enforce a law.

learn.def: to deal with a difficult problem
learn.example: The city must tackle the problem of air pollution.

learn.def: to limit or control something harmful
learn.example: Higher taxes could curb emissions.

learn.def: to start to deal with a matter
learn.example: Leaders must address the issue of housing.

learn.def: to encourage something to develop
learn.example: The summit fostered cooperation between rivals.

learn.def: to put a plan into action
learn.example: The council will implement the policy next year.

learn.def: to make people obey a law
learn.example: Inspectors enforce the law on waste.

learn.def: to put money into something to get benefits later
learn.example: We should invest in public transport.

learn.def: to pay part of the cost to lower the price
learn.example: The state subsidises solar panels.

learn.def: to stop using something gradually
learn.example: Many cities will phase out petrol cars.

learn.def: to make people notice an issue
learn.example: Campaigns raise awareness of plastic waste.

learn.def: to make someone responsible for their actions
learn.example: Polluters must be held accountable.

learn.def: to behave as you want others to behave
learn.example: Governments should lead by example.
